items.title: Bob Marley & The Wailers - Natty Dread (1974)
items.creator: Bob Marley & The Wailers
items.description: Natty Dread is the seventh studio album by Bob Marley & The Wailers, released on October 25, 1974, through Island Records. It marks the first album credited to Bob Marley & The Wailers following the departure of Peter Tosh and Bunny Wailer. Blending socially conscious lyrics with rich reggae grooves and Rastafarian spirituality, the album features timeless songs such as “No Woman, No Cry,” “Lively Up Yourself,” “Revolution,” and “Them Belly Full (But We Hungry).” Natty Dread stands as a cornerstone of reggae music and one of the most influential albums of the 1970s, showcasing Marley’s voice as a global messenger of unity and resistance. This upload is for archival and educational purposes only.

items.title: The Ethel Merman Disco Album
items.creator: Ethel Merman
items.description: American Broadway performer Ethel Merman recorded fourteen songs for the album, although only seven were released on the finished record. Each track was recorded in one take and arranged vocally the way she always did, with disco instrumentation added later as a backtrack. It was originally released by A&M Records in 1979, and the vinyl is considered a collector's item. There's No Business Like Show Business ( Annie Get Your Gun ; Irving Berlin) Everything's Coming Up Roses ( Gypsy ; Jule Styne and Stephen Sondheim) I Get a Kick Out of You ( Anything Goes ; Cole Porter) Something for the Boys ( Something for the Boys ; Porter) Some People ( Gypsy ; Styne and Sondheim) Alexander's Ragtime Band (Berlin) I Got Rhythm (George & Ira Gershwin)

items.title: Panta Rei
items.creator: Panta Rei, Panta Rei
items.description: Panta Rei is attributed to Heraticlus thoughts about change. Πάντα ῥεῖ (panta rei) meaning everything flows in ancient Greek. And this is exactly what you get in this album. Originally issued on the Harvest label in 1973, this is a wonderful stream of trippy Heavy Swedish prog with an intensely groovy jazz-rock & fuzz oriented approach that comes close to Frank Zappa circa “Hot rats”, with some spacey-freaked-out atmospheres and an underlying Canterbury feel. The guitar work is predominant and menacing, whereas the all English lyrics and the rich musical texture that feeds on layers of flutes, maracas, timbales, harmonica and impressive percussion, make for a truly majestic album.

spares.title: Unnamables
spares.creator: univeria zekt, univeria zekt
spares.description: A mythical MAGMA album recorded in 1971, during the “1000 centigrades” period. The album aims at introducing wider audiences to the Zeuhl feel, with a less hermetic sound, favoring a more groovy jazz-rock approach. Features the vocalist of ERGO SUM on one track as well as Tito Puentes on trumpet, otherwise this is pretty much the same line-up as in their previous album. A few dreamy moments with acoustic guitar and flutes (the track “Clementine”), and other typically dense moments with pulsating bass lines, mad sax and weird Vander screams punctuated by furious drumming with a groovy edge

items.title: Prince
items.creator: Prince
items.description: Expanding the urban R&B and funk approach of his debut, Prince is a considerably more accomplished record than his first effort, featuring the first signs of his adventurous sexy signature sound. Although the album is still rather uneven, a handful of songs rank as classics. "I Wanna Be Your Lover" is excellent lite funk and "Why You Wanna Treat Me So Bad?" is a wonderful soulful plea, but "I Feel for You," a sexy slice of urban R&B with a strong pop melody, is the true masterpiece of Prince, indicating the major breakthroughs of his next album, Dirty Mind. [Prince was re-released on LP in 2016.] ~ Stephen Thomas Erlewine (Album review from TiVo)

items.title: Lollipops - Sidste Udkald - På Dansk [Full Album] (1978)
items.creator: Lollipops
items.description: "Sidste Udkald - På Dansk" is the title of the ninth album by the band Lollipops, released under the EMI label in 1978. It features 14 songs and is one of the few albums by the band sung entirely in Danish—unlike their other releases, which were in English—and includes Danish versions of songs originally featured on their 1977 album, "Lollipops City." Fun fact: This album and four others by the band are the only ones where every track is available to listen to online; for the rest, the online tracklists are incomplete, or none of the songs can be heard at all—which is a real shame.
